bugs.what: Regent Ysolde's dialogue menu shrinks as questions are asked, so a later option keeps the same number a different, more consequential option used to have. Re-pressing option 6 out of habit (meaning to ask 'the Hearthlands' tithe') actually fired 'bury the burn-order (breaks the oath)', permanently failing the Marshal's quest and costing Vell -1 regard, with no confirmation prompt for an irreversible, oath-breaking action.
bugs.where: Marrowgate / The Regent's Chambers, talk to Regent Ysolde

bugs.what: No item or action heals a companion outside specific hearths. After the honour guard fight Brother Osk was left at 2/8 hp; every 'use X' consumable (dried herbs, wild herbs, tithe-bread, dried peas) healed only me, and the only party-wide heal found all game was 'rest by the fire' at the Last Light Inn. Deep in the palace crypts, far from any hearth, a companion can be stranded critically wounded with no way to help them.
bugs.where: Marrowgate / The Old Crypts (after fighting the honour guard)

bugs.what: The Free Companies' smuggler route (Grain Run for Sparrow -> Sack Road Camp -> Gullhaven's smugglers' stair/cave/cleft) silently skips Hollowbrook, Cinderhall, Fenmarch and Thornwold -- the exact holds each of the four companions' personal grief-quests point to -- with no confirmation prompt. The only signal is companion banter at the Smugglers' Cleft ('Hollowbrook's behind us... Cinderhall's behind us...'); the explicit system warning ('A companion's grief left unfinished there stays unfinished unless you walk back for it.') only appears afterward, at the Pass Gate, once the skip has already happened.
bugs.where: Saltkerns / The Smugglers' Cleft and The Pass Gate

bugs.what: The Hearthlands' Tally-Sticks quest (collect Sela's stick, the almonry's tally, and the widow's family stick, 3/3) never connects to an action that settles the Hunger Barn's grief -- the grief's own 'weigh' text only ever lists the bargain routes (persuade/force/alter/pay) and the burn route; there is no 'read the sticks aloud' option anywhere, even though Sela's own line implies one should exist ('A bargain isn't a reading. The sticks stay unread... I notice the difference').
bugs.where: Hearthlands / The Hunger Barn, 'weigh what this grief asks'

bugs.what: Rites at Night's own quest text promises four resolutions ('Pay her fine, argue her oath, break her out -- or leave her to it') but the cell's menu only ever offered two of them (force the gate / pick the lock) plus 'leave her to the Watch' -- 'pay her fine' and 'argue her oath' never appeared as selectable options.

The barn-reeve's shade -- the ghost the Hunger Barn's whole grief quest is about -- has no new dialogue after the grief is bargained, even though I retrieved his own chest, his own order, and used it to strike the bargain in his name. Revisiting shows the identical pre-resolution lines.
bugs.where: Hearthlands / The Hunger Barn -- the Loft (after settling the grief)

bugs.what: 'Get your bearings' reports straight-line distance/direction to named landmarks even when the current room has no exit in that direction (e.g. at The Cross-Furrow, bearings said Tithing was '1 south and 2 east' but the room's only exits were N/W/E).
bugs.where: Hearthlands fields / The Cross-Furrow, 'get your bearings'

bugs.what: The Full Measure's room text names 'a landlord who has heard every complaint about the tithe there is to hear' but offers no talk-to option and no named NPC -- the only character mentioned in flavor text with zero interactivity found in the whole hold.

After the Hunger Barn's grief was bargained and the granary opened, only Sergeant Rook and Sela had dedicated reaction lines; Sister Winnow (the almoner who literally decides who eats), Lay-brother Emmet, Peg and Sparrow -- all closer to the grain economy the bargain changed -- had no acknowledgment at all.
bugs.where: Hearthlands / Tithing (The Almonry, The Back Lane) after 'the Hunger Barn, now it's bargained'

bugs.what: Deep companion backstory-and-item dialogue ('ask what they're hiding' / 'ask what really drives her' / 'ask what she's not saying') only unlocked for Vell, Tamsin and Lys (regard +2 or higher); Brother Osk, at regard +1 in the same room, had no equivalent option, with no on-screen indicator anywhere of what regard threshold unlocks it.
bugs.where: Hearthlands / The Hunger Barn -- the Loft, 'speak with the company'

bugs.what: Quartermaster Coll's toll scene is tagged '(hostile, holds its ground, will hear you out)' but no path there is actually violent unless the player deliberately picks the attack option -- pay/slip/talk/Envoy-offer are all peaceful, so the hostile tag reads as a false alarm.
bugs.where: Hearthlands / the Sack Road Camp -- fire

bugs.what: The one Envoy-marked action that produced a flat non-event all game: 'turn your best charm on him (a gamble) (as an Envoy)' on the hunter returned only 'he answers exactly as plainly as before you started', with no visible roll, gain or loss -- every other Envoy-tagged action (Sack Road toll, the hedge-hermit, Herald Corvane, the honour guard's rest-rite) gave a clear win, a clear costed loss, or new content.
bugs.where: Vale of Ash / Hunter's Camp, talk to hunter

bugs.what: 'Travel to a known place' disappeared from the menu at The Empty Seat (the post-resolution Throne of the Barrow) even though it was available one room away on both sides; had to walk down manually to resume fast travel.
bugs.where: Vale of Ash / The Empty Seat

bugs.what: Two unrelated NPCs share the name Sela (the Hearthlands' tally-keeper in Tithing, and a jailed Church novice in Marrowgate's Watch House), which is mildly confusing when cross-referencing status text and journal entries later.
bugs.where: Hearthlands / The Tally-Keeper's Cottage vs Marrowgate / The Watch House Cells

confusions: The Widow's Croft subplot and the Hunger Barn grief are mechanically separate quests resolved by the same NPC (Bailiff Vance) in the same room in consecutive turns, with their dialogue options interleaved in one menu -- easy to conflate as a single quest.

'Hollows rested (holds only; a bargain counts): 1/10' reads ambiguously on first sight (does the 1 include the bargain or not?); the game also shows a separate 'Hollows bargained: 1/10' line that restates the same fact once it applies.

The Hunger Barn's doors read 'barred from within' and 'listen at the doors' returns the identical 'nothing... whatever is still here doesn't make sound' both before and after the grief is bargained -- coherent in hindsight (a bargain isn't a rest) but not obviously distinguished from a stale line on first encounter.

Promising the reeve to seal the barrow (turn 8) locked out the priest's blessing later, and the only place that consequence was explained was the innkeep's aside minutes afterward ('Ask his blessing before promising the reeve... Promise first, and he wants his own way past it') -- a blind player has no way to know the ordering matters until after committing.
It's never made clear in the UI what regard threshold unlocks a companion's deep-backstory dialogue; it appears to be roughly +2, discovered only by comparing four companions side by side.
suggestions: Guard dialogue menus against reused numbers pointing at a different, higher-stakes option once earlier choices are removed from the list (or require a confirm on any 'breaks the oath'/irreversible option).
Let carried food/herb items heal a wounded companion (or auto-share a portion on use), not just the player, so a low-hp ally isn't stranded between hearths.
Before the Sack Road Camp / Smugglers' Cleft shortcut actually skips holds, show the Pass Gate's 'a companion's grief left unfinished stays unfinished' warning up front, with a yes/no confirmation.
Wire the Hearthlands' collected tally-sticks into an actual 'read them aloud' resolution at the Hunger Barn, or adjust Sela's closing line so it stops implying a missing option.
Give the barn-reeve's shade at least one new line once the grief is bargained, mirroring the reactions Sergeant Rook and Sela already got.
Have 'get your bearings' only cite directions that have a real exit from the current room, or state plainly that it ignores walls.
Add reaction lines for Sister Winnow, Sparrow, Emmet and Peg once the granary opens, since they're the NPCs closest to the tithe economy it changed.
Give the Full Measure's 'landlord' an actual talk-to entry or drop the mention from the room text.
Make 'pay her fine' and 'argue her oath' actually reachable for the jailed novice, or trim the quest text down to the two paths that exist.
Drop the 'hostile' tag on Quartermaster Coll (or any NPC) when every actual resolution path is peaceful unless the player initiates violence.
Give the hunter's Envoy 'charm' gamble a visible roll and a real win/lose outcome to match every other Envoy-tagged action in the game.
